title: Pump moved from throttling to a variable speed drive, measured inputs only
grade: Screening grade: 2 of 2 constants are public typical values, not your site's; the measured inputs are as entered and have not been checked.
assumptions: Your electricity energy price equals the public typical value used (0.0851 $/kWh). National or generic figures can differ a great deal from a single site's.
Your grid emission factor equals the public typical value used (0.3496671 kg CO2e/kWh). National or generic figures can differ a great deal from a single site's.
Pump P-101 on a variable speed drive: the kW figures are the average load over the whole year's running, at the same production rate before and after, not a single spot reading.
Pump P-101 on a variable speed drive: the change applies for 8,000 h/yr.
Pump P-101 on a variable speed drive: one energy price applies to every kWh saved (no time-of-use periods, tiers or riders).
Pump P-101 on a variable speed drive: Scope 2 uses a grid average (location-based) factor; the generation that actually backs off at the margin can emit more or less.
Where a range is entered, the result carries both ends. That is the spread of what was entered, not a probability interval.
to_firm_up: Replace the public electricity energy price. Your electricity bill and rate schedule: the energy charge per kWh in the hours the change applies (weight time-of-use periods by the hours saved in each). Not total bill / total kWh, which mixes in demand and fixed charges.

Replace the public grid emission factor. Location-based Scope 2: the EPA eGRID total output emission rate (CO2e) for your eGRID subregion; find the subregion by ZIP code in EPA's Power Profiler, then read the rate from the eGRID summary tables. Market-based Scope 2 instead uses your utility's published supplier-specific emission factor or your contract instruments (RECs, PPAs). Subregion rates differ about 5 times.

Confirm by measurement: Average electrical input kW before and after (or the kW reduction): a clamp-on three-phase power meter, the drive or MCC power reading, or the historian's motor kW tag, over a representative period at the same production rate. An estimate from curves (pump/fan curve and affinity laws) must say so.
Confirm by measurement: Operating hours per year the change applies: historian run status, the operating schedule, or maintenance records. Not 8,760 unless it really runs all year.
After the change, measure the same quantities again at the same production rate: that before/after pair, not this estimate, is the saving.

electricity_price_per_kwh.label: PUBLIC TYPICAL VALUE, replace with your own: 0.0851 $/kWh (US EIA Electric Power Annual Table 2.4, industrial, 2025)
electricity_price_per_kwh.source: US EIA, Electric Power Annual, Table 2.4 Average Price of Electricity to Ultimate Customers by End-Use Sectors, 2015 through 2025, row 2025, 'Total Electric Industry', column Industrial: 8.51 cents per kilowatthour. Data for 2025, released October 21, 2026.
electricity_price_per_kwh.license: Public domain (EIA: 'U.S. government publications are in the public domain', https://www.eia.gov/about/copyrights_reuse.php)
electricity_price_per_kwh.note: An average revenue per kWh (energy, demand and fixed charges together) across all US industrial customers. Your marginal energy rate can differ a great deal by state, utility, tariff and time of day.

grid_kg_co2e_per_kwh.label: PUBLIC TYPICAL VALUE, replace with your own: 0.3496671 kg CO2e/kWh (US EPA eGRID2023 Summary Tables rev. 2, Table 1, U.S. total output CO2e rate, 2023)
grid_kg_co2e_per_kwh.source: US EPA, eGRID2023 Summary Tables (Revision 2), Table 1 Subregion Output Emission Rates, row 'U.S.', total output emission rate CO2e (sheet 'Table 1', cell G32).
grid_kg_co2e_per_kwh.note: Location-based Scope 2 (average emission rate of generation on the grid). Not a market-based factor and not a marginal (avoided-emissions) rate. Excludes transmission and distribution losses (eGRID lists a separate grid gross loss, 4.2% for the U.S.). Subregion total output CO2e rates in the same table run from 242.776 lb/MWh (NYUP, NPCC Upstate NY) to 1,248.582 lb/MWh (SRMW, SERC Midwest) in the contiguous US, about 5 times, and to 1,548.530 lb/MWh (PRMS, Puerto Rico Miscellaneous). Use your subregion, found by ZIP code in EPA's Power Profiler: https://www.epa.gov/egrid/power-profiler

changes.change: Pump P-101 on a variable speed drive

limits: An estimate from the inputs shown, not a measured or verified saving. It is only as good as the measured kW, flow and hours; a before/after measurement at the same production rate is the proof.
Electricity cost uses one energy price per kWh. Tariffs vary (time-of-use, tiers, riders, power factor); demand charges count only when the reduction lowers the billing peak.

Electricity CO2e is location-based Scope 2 (grid average factor given). Market-based Scope 2 uses your supplier's factor or contract instruments and can differ greatly; avoided emissions on the margin also differ.
No savings come from a drawing alone: every quantity here was measured or supplied by the user.
